headline: Both seats get the arcade's three buttons
lede: Missile Command's hot-seat keeps the 1980 law all the way across the board: a human at seat 2 now fires the LEFT, CENTER and RIGHT batteries with Z/X/C, exactly as seat 1 does with 1/2/3 — the board wears the triangle of whoever holds duty, and the join moment teaches it.

notes.text: Z/X/C name the batteries for seat 2 — launched from their own silos (origins 40/400/760), each spending only its own magazine; dead or empty stays a dud, never a reroute. Off-duty presses join the seat but the shot is swallowed, mirroring P1's duty guard. Desktop keyboard only — phones keep the single pad.
The HUD teaches duty: batteries wear 1/2/3 while P1 holds the board and Z/X/C while a human holds seat 2; the PLAYER 2 JOINED card gained a cyan teaching line for the new triangle.

missilecmdcheck 170→182 (§p2-batteries seat-law sim pins + 8 wiring pins), 6 named mutants (53, all die), new mcp2battdrive 16/16 in real Chrome — join, teach pixels, off-duty sleep, per-magazine spend, one-seed byte-equal replay, zero errors.

Honest-gap hygiene: the gunner deep-wave ceiling (#3711's measured law) and the unsourced per-battery arcs (Wikipedia checked; inventing angles is forbidden) are now marked BLOCKED with their evidence — Missile Command's never-dry score lands at 0, so the weakest-title kick moves on instead of re-scoring concluded prose.

look.text: Two players, one keyboard: press 2, hand the board over, and call batteries…
